To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the dispersion of mark-ups across procurement auctions is positively correlated with differences in the availability of cash-flow; (ii) the availability of cash-flows is a significant determinant of the level of mark-ups; (iii) in the absence of private information, mark-ups can take on a wide range of values, from zero to a high value, depending on the availability of cash flows.
the availability of financial constraints matters a lot for the outcome of auctions.

the availability of financial capital matters for the dispersion of mark-ups and the size of money left on the table, that the availability of capital is endogenous and depends on the size of budgets, that the availability and size of capital is a function of the opportunity cost of capital, that the availability is not necessarily a monotonic function of the opportunity costs of capital and that the dispersion of mark-up and money left on the tables is an increasing function of the availability of capital.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of markets in which firms compete for procurement contracts and the financial resources they need to compete.
the role of financial constraints in determining the dynamics of bidding markets.
the impact of financial constraints on bidding behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
financial constraints matter in bidding markets.
our model is not a good fit for the data.
the standard model is a good approximation of reality in some cases but not in general, and that it is not a good approximation of the data in the aggregate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
financial constraints matter for the dynamics of bidding markets and that the empirical literature has not been able to fully capture their effects.
the standard auction model is not a good approximation to the dynamics of bidding markets.
financial constraints are important to explain the dynamics and the dispersion of mark-ups in bidding markets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of bidding markets are driven by the interaction between financial resources and the opportunity cost associated with the use of financial resources.
the availability of financial constraints is a key driver of the observed dynamics of bidding markets.
the availability of financial means is an important determinant of the outcome of procurement markets.
